fields.Name: IT71 - Task Graph Orchestration
fields.Description: Deterministic coverage of the unified workflow DAG engine (plan PR #3456), bundle 'task-graph-orchestration', TG1-TG16. TG1: the six Phase 1 Task columns (InputPayload, OutputPayload, ErrorMessage, AgentRunID, ClaimedBy, ClaimExpiresAt) are present in entity metadata. TG2: those columns round-trip through BaseEntity — write, reload, read back — proving the migration and CodeGen agree. TG3: AIAgentRunStep.StepType accepts the new 'TaskGraph' value, which proves the CHECK-constraint drop-and-re-add was picked up rather than silently skipped. TG4: a cyclic graph is rejected by TaskGraphService naming the cycle, and persists nothing — before the engine work a cycle persisted happily and then deadlocked silently, with the parent marked Complete. TG5: a graph naming an unknown agent is rejected rather than executing with holes; previously the unresolvable task was logged and SKIPPED, producing silent partial execution. TG6: a valid graph persists parent + children + dependency edges with inputs in the InputPayload column and no legacy __TASK_METADATA__ marker in Description. TG7: the four task-graph Remote Operations (TaskGraph.Submit/.Cancel/.RetryTask/.GetStatus) each have an Active metadata row AND resolve to a server implementation rather than the CodeGen contract-only base — the two failure modes a build cannot catch, a forgotten metadata push and a key typo. NO LLM calls. Mutation-by-design: creates and FK-ordered-deletes its own tagged Tasks, Task Dependencies, and Task Types. TG8-TG13 cover the Phase 3/4/6 additions (opt-in agent set, conditional edges, human tasks, the Workflow Remote Operations, and the entity-binding prerequisites). TG14: saving a workflow with an entity-change trigger writes the WHOLE binding — EntityAction + invocation + AgentID/Static + Data/'Entity Object Data' — and re-saving does not duplicate it; this is the check that would have caught Phase 6 shipping a trigger that knew which agent to run but never which record changed. TG15: a trigger declaring scopeEntityName/scopeRecordID actually narrows the binding via EntityAction.ScopeEntityID/ScopeRecordID — Phase 6 accepted the scope and referenced neither, so a workflow scoped to one record fired on every record. TG16: two workflows watching one entity keep separate bindings pointing at their own agents, and re-saving one finds its own row rather than adding a third. 'Execute Agent' is a single shared action, so both would otherwise land on the same (EntityID, ActionID) pair and the second save would rewrite AgentID — silently repointing workflow A's trigger at workflow B's agent while A still looks configured. Writing a second row required dropping UQ_EntityAction_ActionID_EntityID (V202608080100), which the v5.37.x junction sweep had added outside its own stated scope of pure two-FK junction tables; TG16 is what proves the drop took effect. TG14-TG16 are mutation-class and FK-ordered-delete their own Entity Action rows and owned Scheduled Jobs.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: Malformed graphs are rejected before persistence rather than deadlocking or partially executing; valid graphs persist as parent + children + edges with structured payloads in columns; the Phase 1 schema round-trips; and the task-graph control plane is both published and backed by real implementations.
